**Organization Overview**


GreenLight Fund is a national nonprofit with a local focus that partners with communities to create opportunities for inclusive prosperity.  

  

We facilitate a community\-driven process that matches the local needs of individuals and families not met by existing programs, to organizations with track records of success elsewhere. Working with communities, we identify, invite in and launch proven organizations, providing collaborative support so they can quickly take root and deliver change. Everything we do is designed to remove barriers to inclusive prosperity all too often rooted in racial inequities. Our impact increases exponentially as we address one specific, community\-identified need each year, in each GreenLight site.  

  

To date, we have brought 63 evidence\-based portfolio organizations across 14 sites, invested $41M, and attracted an additional $364M from other funding sources, reaching nearly 1\.3M individuals and families this past year alone.

  

To learn more about the GreenLight Fund, please visit www.greenlightfund.org.

The Manager, Office of the CEO will help strengthen the effectiveness of GreenLight’s Office of the CEO by supporting planning, coordination, communication, and follow\-through on key organizational priorities. jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer - Heathcare
jobs.description:
The Bedford\-Stuyvesant Family Health Center (BSFHC) is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that serves all of the primary health care needs of families in the heart of North and Central Brooklyn for over 40 years. Our mission is to provide the most professional, courteous and highest quality health care, with dignity, to those we serve, especially the undeserved population, without regard for ability to pay.
  
  

**SUMMARY:**  

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a Cross\-Enterprise Leader that provides leadership and strategic direction for operating units at BSFHC, including Operational Improvement, Network Management, Provider Operations, and Sales \& Marketing. The COO will partner with BSFHC’s President and executive leaders, directors and managers to develop strategies that shape BSFHC’s overall direction, achieve the organization’s performance goals, and deliver outstanding value for BSFHC’s customers.
  
  

The COO is a leader and innovator of new ideas, ventures and progressive initiatives and will consider the best interests and strategic direction of the entire organization when evaluating department decisions. Enterprise leaders will use their influence to work collaboratively across the organization to initiate and maintain relationships and resolve conflicts. Enterprise leaders will be comfortable dealing with ambiguity, uncertainty, complexity and time pressures, while leveraging these relationships.
  
  

**Duties and Responsibilities include but not limited to:**  

* Accept delegated areas of administration. Responsible for efficient practices and maximize productivity in all areas as defined by the CEO.
* Provides operational oversight and creates mechanisms to monitor infrastructure, processes and standards to achieve desired outcomes as part of corporate business plan and strategic initiatives.
* Collaborates with Leadership to set goals, clearly define operations, and develop appropriate performance standards, metrics and reporting tools.
* Develops, implements and manages the operations budget ensuring effective stewardship of resources, and achievement of Strategic Operating Plan (SOP) goals and annual corporate goals.
* Sets vision and leads operational departments by directing and coordinating activities consistent with established goals, compliance and quality requirements, objectives and policies and procedures.
* Develops short and long term strategies and tactics to assure operational and programmatic excellence, management and control.
* Develops and implements strategies to deliver superior Customer Service, Enrollment and Claims Administration to members and providers.
* Initiates, implements and monitors improvement activities aimed at reducing costs, increasing accuracy and efficiency and both internal and external customer satisfaction in each operational area.
* Analyze systems and procedures and recommend changes to improve workflow and efficiency.
* Prepare assigned areas for Joint Commission, DOH and HRSA Surveys
* Responsible for Emergency Preparedness, Fire Drills and PCEPN
* Interpret clinic policies, objectives and operational procedures to department heads.
* Resolve problems relating to utilization of facilities, equipment and supplies.
* Represent the Center at public and professional meetings and conferences as requested.
* Responsible for MIS system personnel and equipment placements
* Maintain professional affiliations and enhance professional development to keep pace with the trends in health care administration.
* Assist the Chief Executive Officer with planning, directing and coordinating facility activities to ensure full patient care based on clinic policies.


**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:**  

* Bachelors Degree required
* Masters, MBA, MPH or related post\-graduate degree preferred
* Three years experience in health administration including two years experience in a clinic environment.
* 10\+ years of senior management experience, with a minimum of 5 years leading one or more of the following functions: Customer Service, Claims, Enrollment, Operational Improvement, Value\-Based Contracting, or Sales \& Marketing
* 10\+ years of experience in a managed care/health care environment or a related government program
* Demonstrated experience successfully planning, organizing, managing and implementing Executive level projects


**Related Skills/Experience and requirements:**  

* Experience with government programs and their regulations, guidelines, and standards
* Exceptional executive leadership, strategic and day\-to\-day project and task management
* Demonstrated abilities in: Inductive Reasoning, Data Analytics, Employee Engagement, Conflict Resolution, Marketing Management and Provider Relationships
* Strong organizational and project management skills
* Excellent judgment and creative problem solving skills
* Solid understanding of physician practice operations including charge capture and clinical documentation;
* Outstanding listening and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively work and communicate with providers and practice staff;
* Time management skills and attention to detail;


**Benefits Overview:** We offer attractive compensation with comprehensive benefits including: Medical, 401k Retirement Plan with discretionary Match, Free Life Insurance and Long\-Term Disability, Transportation Plan, Generous Paid Vacations and Holidays.
  
  

**Salary:** 100k and based on experience

This role is intentionally designed as a focused part\-time leadership position. The Associate Executive Director will provide senior\-level oversight, strategic partnership, funder stewardship support, and program coordination within a defined scope.


At this stage, the role is not designed to carry full\-time executive responsibility, full ownership of new revenue development, or hands\-on implementation of every operational improvement. Scope may expand over time as the organization grows.

* Full ownership of business development or revenue generation
* Hands\-on implementation of organizational transformation initiatives
* Direct ownership of program content or day\-to\-day program management
* Primary board strategy leadership, which remains with the Executive Director

--------------------------


* 8 or more years of nonprofit leadership experience with progressive responsibility

This is a strong opportunity for a senior nonprofit leader who wants to contribute at a strategic level while working within a defined, part\-time scope. Qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

**The RMP Promise**


Rocky Mountain Prep is a movement of educators, families, scholars, and advocates committed to changing public education in Colorado by democratizing college access for historically marginalized students and families. We operate twelve college\-preparatory schools serving students from early childhood through twelfth grade, and we are fundamentally a world\-class learning organization that invests deeply in every educator who joins us. Teachers engage in ongoing coaching and professional development, supported by clear expectations, transparent feedback, and opportunities to strengthen their craft and advance along individualized career pathways grounded in our PEAK values. Rooted in a culture of rigor and love, RMP promises to coach, develop, and champion every team member so they can do their best work and grow as professionals, people, and leaders.

**About the Role**


Every RMP role ladders up to five organizational priorities. The Managing Director of Financial Partnership sits primarily inside Financial Sustainability, but our budgeting and training work also directly enables Staff Engagement \& Enablement and Student Achievement by giving school leaders and NST (central office) staff the clarity and tools to run strong, financially healthy schools and departments.

**2026–27 DRIVING GOALS FOR THIS ROLE**


Each member of the organization is held accountable for goals that ladder to our network priorities. In this role, you will own the following:

* **Budget Accuracy:** Maintain less than 5% variance between budget and actuals across RMP school and network\-support budgets, with monthly variance analysis and corrective forecasting.
* **Stakeholder Budget Literacy:** Design and deliver an ongoing learning \& development curriculum that builds budget fluency across both school leaders and NST (central office) budget owners — reading, forecasting, and managing their own budgets — measured by leader confidence surveys and reduced budget\-related escalations.
* **Financial Sustainability:** Support the network's enrollment and philanthropy goals (5,100 enrollment / $4M philanthropy) by ensuring campus and grant budgets are accurate, timely, and audit\-ready.
* **Board \& Executive Reporting:** Prepare and, when needed, present clear, board\-ready financial materials that translate complex budget data into decision\-useful narratives for the Board of Directors and executive team.
* **Staff Retention:** Contribute to RMP's 75% staff retention goal by giving school leaders, ops staff, and NST staff the financial clarity and support that reduces operational stress.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Financial Partnership \& Budget Literacy (Learning \& Development)**


This is the anchor of the role: building a network of budget owners — both school leaders and NST (central office) department leads — who are genuinely fluent in their own budgets, not just recipients of reports.

* Design and facilitate a structured budget\-literacy training curriculum for both principals and NST (central office) budget owners, including onboarding training for new leaders and refresher sessions tied to the budget calendar.
* Train principals and NST department leads to read, interpret, and act on their budgets — building their independent capacity to forecast and manage their controlled expenditures.
* Provide monthly reports to principals and NST budget owners on their schools' or departments' year\-to\-date financial performance, paired with a working session (not just a document drop) to build understanding.
* Develop tools, templates, and job aids that make budget forecasting accessible and repeatable for non\-finance leaders across schools and NST.
* Serve as the primary financial partnership point of contact for principals and NST department leads on spending management and financial decision\-making.
* Evaluate the effectiveness of the existing FP\&A process and budget\-management system; identify and implement improvements, including ways to scale training as RMP grows.
* Track and report on budget\-literacy outcomes across school and NST budget owners alike (e.g., leader confidence, self\-service accuracy, reduction in errors) as a core measure of program success.

**Financial Planning \& Analysis**


Assist the MD of Finance and Planning in developing and maintaining the annual budget for RMP schools, including forecasting revenue from public funding, grants, and donations, and managing staffing, district fee, instructional materials, and facilities expenses.

* Prepare monthly P\&L reports for RMP schools and NST, including variance analysis against budget and forecast for the remainder of the year, with a standing target of maintaining variance under 5%.
* Develop monthly salary, variable pay, and substitute\-teacher cost analysis and forecasts.
* Review monthly financial outcomes and discuss risks, opportunities, and variance drivers with the ED of Finance and Planning.
* Build financial models to support ad hoc, network\-level decision\-making.

**Board \& Executive Reporting**

* Translate FP\&A results, variance analysis, and forecasts into clear, board\-ready materials as needed, in partnership with the ED of Finance and Planning.
* Present financial updates to the Board of Directors or executive team when called upon, with the same clarity and "no surprises" standard expected of all RMP leaders.
* Anticipate the questions Board members and executives will ask about variance, sustainability metrics, and grant compliance, and prepare supporting detail in advance.

Bennett College is a historically Black liberal arts college for women in Greensboro, NC. With a 7/1 student/faculty ratio, Bennett provides an intimate, engaging learning community that centers the experiences and achievements of women of color. Traditional events and ceremonies throughout the academic year honor the College’s history and contribute to the holistic development of our students as scholars and leaders.
Bennett College seeks new faculty who can contribute to the development of innovative programs and curricula that prepare students for impactful civic engagement and leadership roles in their personal and professional lives. Prospective public health faculty whose work touches on maternal and child health, health disparities, diversifying STEM/healthcare, public health, and environmental justice are especially encouraged to apply. Bennett College offers the biology major/minor and chemistry minor and is launching majors in public health and health sciences in fall 2026\.  


**GENERAL SUMMARY:**
Bennett’s BSPH curriculum combines an interdisciplinary core with concentration pathways and is distinguished by quantitative rigor, applied public health analytics, and a mission\-driven emphasis on health equity and the health of Black women.
